title: Inaccurate host matching logic in `pkg/api/handlers/compat/auth.go`
body:
`pkg/api/handlers/compat/auth.go` uses `strings.HasPrefix(authConfig.ServerAddress, "https://localhost:")`.

That could plausibly be bypassed using an `https://localhost:password@other-host.example` syntax; at least for cleanliness, we should parse URLs properly (while allowing for non-URLs?).

But first of all, should the special case exist?

comments.body: I would like to drop the special case, the git hisatory just leads to "allow for local testing" but that could just all well be achieved by configuring registry.conf properly which IMO is the correct thing to do.

On the principle of the thing: 

I can see the argument that `localhost` is special and that _for interactive use_, it should have TLS disabled by default.

I think it’s much weaker for API uses of any kind (and c/image nor `docker/distribution` has that special case).

---

… but, really, the primary concern for a compatibility API should be users. Does this break workflows similar to local `compose`, for example?
